name: Bristol Myers Squibb
description: Bristol Myers Squibb discovers, makes and sells prescription medicines, mainly for cancer, blood disorders, immune disease, heart disease and neuroscience, through one reportable segment. It sells principally to wholesalers, distributors and specialty pharmacies. Revenue is split by the company into a Growth Portfolio (newer brands such as Opdivo, Reblozyl, Breyanzi, Camzyos; $26.4 billion, rising 17%) and a Legacy Portfolio (Eliquis, Revlimid, Pomalyst, Sprycel and others; $21.8 billion, falling 15% as generics arrive). Eliquis alone is $14.4 billion gross, a product it develops and sells jointly with Pfizer, which reports only its own share.

employees.note: About 32,500 employees in 43 countries; 54% in the US (excluding Puerto Rico).

businessLines.name: Growth Portfolio
businessLines.how: Sells patented newer brands (cancer immunotherapy, cell therapy, blood, heart and neuroscience medicines) to wholesalers, specialty pharmacies and hospitals; growth from new indications and launches.

businessLines.name: Legacy Portfolio
businessLines.how: Sells older established brands; Eliquis sales are shared-profit with Pfizer, while Revlimid, Pomalyst, Sprycel and Abraxane are losing sales to generics.

brands.name: Eliquis
brands.note: Developed and commercialised jointly with Pfizer; profits and losses are shared equally globally except where Pfizer commercialises and pays BMS a sales-based fee; Pfizer funds 50-60% of development cost.
